use a p-norm approximation with tuned p
use exact subgradient only, no smoothing

proposed.what: All return the best exact-R iterate encountered, not the last iterate or an average of iterates.
All compute the autoconvolution via FFT with power-of-two padding (rfft/irfft or fftconvolve).
All enforce the CPU deadline with time.process_time checks inside callbacks/objectives and return best-so-far.
All represent f as nonnegative step heights on equal-width cells and compute R from L=[0,conv(h,h),0] with the exact piecewise-linear integral.
All maximize R = num/(s^2 * max L) with s=sum(h) and max over all knots, exploiting scale/width invariance.

confirmed.what: All use scipy.optimize.minimize with method L-BFGS-B as the sole local search engine.
alternatives: CMA-ES or Adam-style stochastic local search
confirmed.why: Different curvature/constraint handling changes which local optimum is reached and how fast.

confirmed.what: All keep a single incumbent shape and greedily return the best exact R seen; no population or recombination.
alternatives: maintain a diverse population of shapes
average several nearby optima before polishing
confirmed.why: Recombination or diversity can escape basins that a single incumbent cannot.
